title: Zebrafish Immunofluorescence Protocol
author: Kim Kobar
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.zwif7ce

steps.title: Dechorionate Embryos
steps.instruction: Dechorionate embryos using two pairs of forceps under a dissecting microscope.

substeps.instruction: Pinch the embryo's chorion with one pair of forceps.
Pinch the chorion near the original pinch with the second pair of forceps.
Gently tear the chorion by separating the hands.
Repeat until embryos are dechorionated.

steps.title: Transfer and Label Embryos
steps.instruction: Transfer dechorionated embryos into labeled microcentrifuge tubes using a large bore pipette.

substeps.instruction: Place up to 50 embryos per tube.
Label the top and side of the tube with: number of embryos, age in hpf, injection contents and amount, and injection date.

steps.title: Remove Excess Liquid
steps.instruction: Remove as much liquid as possible from the microcentrifuge tubes using a small bore pipette.

steps.title: Fix Embryos
steps.instruction: Fix embryos in ~1mL of 4% PFA for 1 hour at room temperature (RT) on a rocker.

substeps.instruction: Place tubes on their side, oriented perpendicular to the rocking motion so embryos rock side to side rather than cap to bottom.
Wear gloves when working with PFA.

steps.title: Remove PFA
steps.instruction: Discard PFA from tubes into PFA waste using a small bore pipette, taking care not to damage embryos.

steps.title: Rinse Embryos
steps.instruction: Rinse embryos in ~1mL PBS twice for 5 minutes each at RT on the rocker.

substeps.instruction: Remove solution with a small bore pipette before adding new solution each time.

steps.title: Perform Age-Specific Washing
steps.instruction: Wash embryos based on their age in hours post fertilization (hpf) at RT on the rocker.

substeps.instruction: For 24-48 hpf embryos: Wash in ~1mL DI H2O for 5 min.
For ~72 hpf embryos: Wash 5 min in DI H2O, place in 100% acetone at -20°C for 5 min, then wash in DI H2O again for 5 min.

steps.title: Block Embryos
steps.instruction: Incubate embryos in 500 ul IF Block solution for 1 hour at RT on the rocker.

substeps.instruction: Note: Keep IF Block at 4°C from this point until the 2° Antibody Solution is made on Day 2 to avoid freeze/thaw cycles.

steps.title: Apply Primary Antibody
steps.instruction: Apply the primary antibody solution to the embryos.

substeps.instruction: Remove and discard IF Block solution into a waste beaker.
Add 100 ul per tube of 1° antibody diluted in IF Block solution (refer to dilution table for specific concentrations).
Incubate overnight at 4°C.

steps.title: Wash Primary Antibody
steps.instruction: Remove 1° Antibody Solution and discard in waste beaker. Rinse all day in 100μL-500μL PBS-0.1% Triton at RT on the rocker.

substeps.instruction: Change the solution 3-4 times throughout the day, removing solution before adding new solution.

steps.title: Apply Secondary Antibody
steps.instruction: Apply the secondary antibody solution to the embryos.

substeps.instruction: Remove PBS-0.1% Triton and replace with 100 ul per tube of 2° Antibody Solution.
Dilute secondary antibodies 1:750 in IF block.
Choose Dylight488 (green) for single stain or Dylight 594 (red) for dual stain, matching the species of the primary antibody.
Wrap tubes in tin foil and incubate overnight at 4°C in the dark.

steps.title: Final Rinse and Storage
steps.instruction: Perform final washes and store embryos.

substeps.instruction: Remove solution with a small bore pipette.
Rinse in PBS-0.1% Triton twice for 5 minutes each at RT on the rocker.
Store in at least 200 ul PBS at 4°C.
Image within one week to avoid degradation.
